title: Sirloin Steak with Chimichurri
subtitle: Pan-seared sirloin with a fresh parsley and garlic sauce
excerpt: A quick chimichurri made with parsley, garlic, and red wine vinegar is sharp enough to cut through the richness of a sirloin steak. Make the sauce first so the flavours have time to come together.
sourceNotes: Argentinian chimichurri paired with British sirloin. The sauce is the traditional Argentinian condiment for grilled meat.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Chimichurri keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. A cold steak straight into a hot pan cooks unevenly.
Make the chimichurri. Mix the parsley, garlic, 80ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, oregano, and chilli flakes in a bowl. Season well and set aside.
Pat the steaks dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large frying pan over very high heat until the oil just starts to smoke.
Cook the steaks for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium rare. Do not move them while they are searing.
Remove from the pan. Rest on a warm plate for 5 minutes.
Slice each steak and spoon the chimichurri over the top. Serve with chips or crusty bread.

items.symptom: Steak grey rather than brown on the outside.
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or steak was very wet.
items.fix: Pat very dry with kitchen paper; pan must be smoking before steak goes in.

items.cause: Cooked too long or pieces were thin.
items.fix: For medium rare, 2 minutes per side is usually enough for 2cm-thick steaks.

items.cause: Too much vinegar or not enough oil to balance it.
items.fix: Add more olive oil and a pinch of sugar to round out the acidity.
